_note: Hand-maintained notes on the amending Acts, keyed by instrument_id. The parser never edits the source wording; anything wrong in the print is recorded here instead, so the tree keeps saying what the Act says and the reader still learns what is off about it. Mirrors data/processed/canonical-overrides.json, which does the same for the principal statutes.

quality_notes: The Government Printer PDF is a 4-page scan with no text layer, so this tree is parsed from an offline OCR reading. Wording has not been proof-read against the scan.

This is a 1958 Government Press print. The OCR reads its quotation marks as letter pairs throughout -- an opening quote as '<c', '<6', 'c6', 'cc' or 'c<' and a closing quote as '>>', '3>', '>.' or ',9'. Every quoted extract in the body is affected. The wording between the marks is generally sound; the marks themselves are not.
Marginal notes and the provision interleave in this print, so several section headings carry fragments of the note's column out of order. See known_ocr_defects.

Running headers and the printer's imprint fall inside section 2's text ('1-J N. R 21 670-2 775 (2/5S) 4 Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act, No. 22 of 1958'). They are page furniture, not part of the provision.

quality_notes: The Government Printer PDF is an 11-page scan with no text layer, so this tree is parsed from an offline OCR reading. Wording has not been proof-read against the scan.
This tree is the least reliable of the six in the package and should not be relied on before it is proof-read. The damage is structural, not just spelling: see known_ocr_defects.

The body carries duplicate section numbers. Two further nodes numbered 1 and 2 appear after section 5, produced by the Form VIII / Form X specimen text of the Second Schedule being read as numbered sections. They are schedule forms, not sections of the Act.

Several section headings have swallowed whole runs of body text where the marginal-note column was not separated cleanly. Section 2's heading in particular runs to roughly a page of the substituted section 32(1).

Common letter substitutions through the body: 'thc' for 'the', 'thercof' for 'thereof', 'repcal' for 'repeal', 'scction' for 'section', 'hcreinafter' for 'hereinafter', 'Attomey' for 'Attorney', 'wiuness' for 'witness', 'LO' for 'to', 'Actmayl' for 'Act may', 'isnott' for 'is not'.

21-2013.checked_against: Government Printer PDF, Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act, No. 21 of 2013, certified 24th April 2013
quality_notes: Parsed from the Government Printer PDF's own text layer, not from OCR. Every word of the source is accounted for in the tree (0.00% unmatched by scripts/check_parse_coverage.py). The defects below are structural -- text placed in the wrong node -- not lost or misread wording.

Section 5 does not appear in the body as its own node. On page 2 the print mirrors the usual Government Printer layout and runs the marginal note down the LEFT column with the provision on the right, which is the regime scripts/parse_amendment_pdf.py expects only inside quoted extracts. Section 5 and its note were therefore read as a continuation of section 4. Its full text -- 'The First Schedule of the principal enactment is hereby amended as follows' and limbs (1)(i), (1)(ii), (1)(iii) and (2) -- is present inside section 4's text.

The body carries duplicate section numbers. Three nodes numbered 1, 2 and 3 appear after section 4; they are the numbered fee items of the Part III table that section 5 substitutes into the First Schedule, not sections of the Act.
Because section 5 is not a node, no amendment instruction is recorded for the First Schedule. The Act does amend it. Read section 4's text, not the instruction list, for that change.
Section 7's text runs on into the back-cover imprint of the printed pamphlet ('Payable to the SUPERINTENDENT, GOVERNMENT PUBLICATIONS BUREAU ...'). That is page furniture, not part of the provision.

This tree was first built through Git Bash, where pdftotext resolves to an Xpdf 4.00 build that ignores '-enc UTF-8'; the result lost every curly quote and em dash to U+FFFD and dropped three further sections. It was rebuilt through PowerShell, where pdftotext resolves to poppler 25.07. Rebuild this tree from PowerShell.
